priorReviewerFeedback:
ATTEMPT 1 CRITIC
## Critique
- claim-1: Supported by the cited excerpt. However, these lines alone do not supply the quotient presentation, admissible parameter ranges, or Schur-basis conventions needed for the proposed relation matrices.
- claim-2: Correctly distinguishes finite verification from a universal proof. The strategy preserves this limitation.
- claim-3: Supported and directly relevant. Its application requires checking that the ideal structure in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) agrees with the asserted graded \(\Lambda\)-module structure and that the listed generators are homogeneous.
- claim-4: The conditional argument is valid. The remaining applicability audit should not be overstated: source-2@L1536-L1540 already states that \(\Lambda\) is the connected graded ring of symmetric functions, \(M=J_v\), and the quotient is finitely generated. What remains missing is enough formal context to construct and verify the proposed presentations.
- claim-5: Supported. The strategy nevertheless makes the stronger target unnecessarily difficult. Since \(Q_v\) is already spanned by \(N\) elements, proving
  \[
  \dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q_v\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q)=N
  \]
  makes the surjection \(\mathbb Z^N\to Q_v\) injective and therefore proves \(Q_v\cong\mathbb Z^N\). A separate torsion-freeness proof is unnecessary. By contrast, dimension \(N\) modulo one prime proves minimal generator number \(N\) but not freeness.
- claim-6: Must remain restricted to the supplied search materials. It does not establish that no relevant theorem exists in the literature.
- The matrix step is underspecified. It should define
  \[
  (Q_v)_d=(J_v)_d\Big/\sum_{k>0}\Lambda_k(J_v)_{d-k},
  \]
  identify integral bases or generating lattices for every term, and justify finiteness. A “Schur basis” cannot be assumed without sourcing its behavior in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\).
- The proposed bounded computation has no explicit parameter bound, matrix artifact, Smith-normal-form output, or executed computation record. It therefore supplies no computational evidence.
- The literature-search component gives no named theorem with exact hypotheses and no precise reduction target. A useful target would be a theorem computing indecomposables \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), equivalently \(\operatorname{Tor}^{\Lambda}_0(\mathbb Z,J_v)\), or the corresponding graded Betti numbers.
- The independent-review checkpoint is only prospective. No independent-review record accompanies the notation audit or matrices, so the acceptance criterion is not yet met.
- Overall, the strategy acknowledges the reviewer concern but does not resolve it: it neither retrieves an applicable literature theorem nor completes the algebraic lower bound.

## Required revisions
- Replace the rank-plus-torsion target with the sharper lemma: an abelian group spanned by \(N\) elements is \(\mathbb Z^N\) if its rational rank is \(N\). Reduce the problem to rational linear independence of either displayed list in \(Q_v\).
- Complete the notation audit using exact formal locators for \(I_{r,n-r}\), the grading, the \(\Lambda\)-action, the admissible partitions, and the homogeneous ideal \(J_v\).
- Give a precise finite presentation of each \((Q_v)_d\), including all product maps \(\Lambda_k\otimes(J_v)_{d-k}\to(J_v)_d\) and the quotient relations inherited from \(I_{r,n-r}\).
- Specify an exact bounded parameter family and provide actual matrices and computation records; label their conclusions as finite evidence only.
- Conduct a theorem-focused literature search for indecomposables, minimal graded generators, or \(\operatorname{Tor}^{\Lambda}_0(\mathbb Z,J_v)\). Record exact theorem statements and hypotheses before claiming applicability.
- Obtain an independent review of the resulting maps, bases, and finite computations. Until then, both the universal minimality claim and the literature reduction remain unresolved.

sources.title: Model Reduction for Switched Differential-Algebraic Equations with Known Switching Signal
sources.summary: Building on our recently proposed model reduction methods for switched ordinary linear systems, we propose a comprehensive model reduction method for linear switched differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). In contrast to most other available model reduction methods for switched systems, we consider the switching signal as a given time-variance of the system. This allows us to exploit certain linear subspaces in the reduction process and also provide in general significantly smaller reduced models compared to methods which consider arbitrary switching signals. Model reduction for switched DAEs has some unique features that make a generalization of the available methods nontrivial; in particular, the presence of jumps and Dirac impulses in response to switches have to be carefully treated. Furthermore, due to the algebraic constraints, the reachability subspaces cannot be the full space, hence a straightforward application of balanced truncation is not possible (because the corresponding reachability Gramians will be structurally non-invertible). We resolve this problem by first applying an exact model reduction which reduces the switched DAE to a switched ordinary system with jumps and which carefully keeps track of the impulsive effects. As a second step, we then apply a midpoint balanced truncation approach to further reduce the switched system. In addition to the challenge to appropriately take into account the Dirac impulses, another novel challenge was the occurrence of input-dependent state-jumps. We propose to deal with input-dependent jumps by combining certain discrete-time reachability Gramians with continuous-time reachability Gramians. We provide corresponding Matlab implementations of the proposed algorithms and illustrate their effectiveness with some academic examples.

sources.title: Living Interactive Design: Towards Architectural Environments Responsive to User Biodata
sources.summary:
In the modern era, technological advancements are progressing rapidly, leading to the emergence of a new 
concept in architectural design known as "Living Interactive Design." This approach aims to create 
intelligent and flexible architectural environments that respond directly to user data, thereby providing 
personalized experiences that enhance comfort and address individual needs. Living Interactive Design 
relies on collecting vital user data—such as heart rate, temperature, movement, and other environmental 
signals—and transforming this information into immediate environmental responses. For example, a 
building might adjust the lighting, temperature, or even music based on the user’s mood or activity. This 
paradigm represents a significant step toward developing smarter and more adaptable architectural 
environments, which continuously interact with users in real-time. It contributes to improving quality of 
life, increasing efficiency, and fostering human-environment interaction. Additionally, such designs 
facilitate energy consumption reduction and promote environmental sustainability through automatic 
adaptation to environmental conditions and changes in space usage. In summary, research in the field of 
Living Interactive Design seeks to offer innovative solutions that integrate technology and architecture, 
creating architectural environments that respond in a simple yet effective manner to user data. These 
environments aim to provide more personalized and flexible living experiences. This trend reflects a 
forward-looking vision based on ongoing, dynamic interaction between humans and their surrounding 
environment, opening new horizons toward more intelligent and sustainable architectural design.This study 
aims to explore and develop the concept of live interactive design for architectural environments that 
respond dynamically and instantly to users' vital data. To achieve this, an integrated methodology has been 
adopted, combining a review of scientific literature with the analysis of applied case studies, with the goal 
of building a comprehensive theoretical and practical framework that contributes to the development of 
design models based on live data.

sources.title: not-yet-known not-yet-known not-yet-known unknown DEMOGRAPHIC TURNOVER IN SOCIAL NETWORKS: NEW RECRUITS CREATE COMMUNITIES, RETURNING INDIVIDUALS CREATE CONNECTIONS
sources.summary: Animal social structure is influenced by demographic processes such as survival and recruitment. Yet, how the gain and loss of social associations among individuals scale up through levels of social organization is poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted multiscale analysis of long-term social network dynamics over twelve winters for a migrant passerine, the golden-crowned sparrow. We found consistently high levels of stability in pairwise associations among returning sparrows, but this social fidelity was not the strongest driver of higher-level properties such as community cohesion and network modularity. Instead, these were increased more by the clustered social associations of newly immigrating individuals. Thus, the interplay of distinct processes---social fidelity among older birds and social cohesion among newer birds---jointly drive social structures at different levels of social organization. Our results demonstrate the different effects of demographic changes on social structure across pairwise, community, and population levels.

117: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
118: 
119: %The first main result of this paper is Theorem 1.1 below.  We first
120: %explain here some of the background and motivation behind it.
121: % AY: I know we've talked about this before, but given there's an abstract,
122: % this sentence seems a little funny to me. What else were we planning to do
123: % but to explain the background and motivation for our result?
124: 
125: The cohomology of the generalized flag manifold $G/B$, for any complex
126: semisimple algebraic group $G$ and Borel subgroup $B$, has a classical
127: presentation due to Borel \cite{Borel}.  Pick a maximal torus
128: $T\subset B\subset G$, choose a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero, and let
129: $V=\Bbbk\otimes_{\ZZ} X(T)$, where $X(T)$ is the coweight lattice of
130: $T$.  Let $\Bbbk[V]:=\Sym(V^{\star})$ be the symmetric algebra for
131: $V^{\star}$; it naturally carries an action of the Weyl group $W :=
132: N_G(T)/T$.  Furthermore let $\Bbbk[V]^W$ be the ring of $W$-invariants
133: of $\Bbbk[V]$, and $\Bbbk[V]^W_+$ the ideal of $\Bbbk[V]$ generated by
134: the $W$-invariants of positive degree.  A classical theorem of Borel
135: \cite{Borel} states that
136: \begin{equation}
137: \label{Borel-presentation}
138: H^*(G/B,\Bbbk) \cong \Bbbk[V]/(\Bbbk[V]^W_+).
139: \end{equation}
140: %This presentation is proved by showing that $\Bbbk[V]^W_+$ is the kernel of the
141: %surjective map $\Sym(V^\star) \rightarrow H^*(G/B)$ that sends a torus
142: %weight $\lambda \in V^{\star}$ to the first Chern class of the equivariant
143: %line bundle ${\mathcal L}_\lambda$ on $G/B$; see the original paper
144: %\cite{Borel} or, e.g., \cite[\S III.4]{Hiller} for further details.  
145: 
146: A desirable feature of Borel's presentation is its shortness: since $W$
147: acts on $V^\star$ as a finite reflection group, by Chevalley's Theorem,
148: the $W$-invariants $\Bbbk[V]^W$ are a polynomial algebra
149: $\Bbbk[f_1,\ldots,f_n]$, where $n:=\dim_\Bbbk V$ is the rank of
150: $G$ \cite[Section~3.5]{humphreys}.  Hence Borel's presentation shows
151: that $H^\star(G/B)$ is a complete intersection as it has $n$ generators and
152: $n$ relations.
153: 
154:  There is a second way to describe $H^{\star}(G/B)$ arising from
155:  a cell decomposition of $G/B$. One has
156: $$
157: \begin{array}{rll}
158: G&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} BwB & \text{(Bruhat decomposition)}\\
159: G/B&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} X_w^\circ & \text{(Schubert cell decomposition), with}\\ 
160: X_w^\circ&:=BwB/B \cong \CC^{\ell(w)} &\text{ (open Schubert cell)}.
